changes: p2: re-segmented 'jyānilajyā śaṃkarasyedaṃ' as 'jyānī lajyāśaṃkarasya': owner's name is Lajyāśaṃkara (= Lajjāśaṅkara, a common Gujarati name), and Jyānī (= Jānī, a Gujarati brahmin surname) goes into titles. Confidence lowered to medium.
Removed the wrote_for relation p1→p2. The colophon does not say the scribe wrote the copy for the owner; the ownership statement could have been added later.

notes: 'jyānilajyā śaṃkarasyedaṃ' is best read as 'jyānī lajyāśaṃkarasyedaṃ': Jānī (a Gujarati brahmin surname) + Lajjāśaṅkara (a typical Gujarati personal name). The alternative split 'Śaṃkara' cannot be ruled out. The names Dadhīca, Jānī and Lajjāśaṅkara suggest the copy was made in western India (Gujarat/Rajasthan), not Nepal. The colophon does not say whether the owner commissioned the copy. 'rāma rāma' is an invocation, not a person. Ends with the usual scribal verse 'bhagnapṛṣṭhakaṭigrīvā...'. VS 1840 Kārtika kṛṣṇa 5 falls in Oct/Nov 1783 CE; the weekday was not checked.
